newsitem.title: USA: Suspect in Ohio fireworks deaths said incompetent.
newsitem.headline: Suspect in Ohio fireworks deaths said incompetent.

text.p: A brain-damaged man suspected of touching off a fireworks store blaze in July that killed nine people was declared incompetent to stand trial Wednesday and sent to a psychiatric hospital for treatment.

Lawrence County Judge Richard Walton agreed with a psychological evaluation that Todd Hall would need at least a year of treatment to become competent to stand trial. Hall, 24, had a partial lobotomy in 1987 after a skateboarding accident.

Hall allegedly set off firecrackers in a fireworks store in nearby Scottown on July 3, sparking a blaze that killed four children and five adults. Last month, he pleaded innocent by reason of insanity to nine counts of involuntary manslaughter and four counts of aggravated arson.
